Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-5767D9118E-71989
Notice Date: 2026-08-09
Requested Service: Partial knee replacement (CPT 27446)
Treating Surgeon: Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 (partial knee replacement), communicated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-09. The stated reason for denial was: "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure."

I disagree with this determination. The notice does not cite a specific policy number, section, or criterion that was applied to reach this conclusion, so I am responding based on the only publicly available CountyCare document I could identify that addresses CPT 27446: "EVH Clinical Guideline 2734.CC for Outpatient Major Joint Arthroplasty (Hips and Knees)" (Guideline Number: EVH_CG_2734.CC; Original Date: January 3, 2022; Last Revised Date: December 9, 2025; Implementation Date: January 1, 2026). If a different or more specific criterion set was actually used to deny this request, I formally request, as part of this appeal, that CountyCare identify that document by name, number, and version, and provide me a copy, as well as the name and credentials of the reviewer who made this determination and a peer-to-peer review opportunity for Dr. Marchetti.

I have not independently verified that this guideline is the correct or complete basis for the denial, and I am not quoting any policy language that I did not retrieve directly from this document. To the extent CountyCare relied on different or additional criteria, I ask that this appeal be evaluated against whatever the correct, governing document actually says.

Response to the stated imaging concern:

The guideline lists, as qualifying findings for "Severe osteoarthritis or bone condition by radiographic or imaging": "Effusions," "Acute fracture," "Avascular necrosis," "Joint space narrowing or large osteophytes on imaging," "Severe sclerosis or deformity," and "Bone on bone contact."

The MRI of the knee performed 2026-05-30 documents "full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition" and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. This finding directly corresponds to "Bone on bone contact" as enumerated in the guideline, and the joint-space loss described is consistent with "Joint space narrowing" as also enumerated. I therefore ask the reviewer to explain, in the appeal determination, specifically why this documented bone-on-bone finding was found insufficient, since it appears to match the guideline's own listed imaging criterion.

Response to other applicable documentation elements:

The same guideline states that "the documentation should include the following criteria in 2 or more areas," including physical exam findings such as "Instability on stress-testing" and "Abnormal or limited range of motion (compared to usual function)," as well as "Interference with ADLS." The submitted records include:

- Physical exam findings of positive provocative testing on the affected knee and range of motion limited by pain, consistent with the exam findings referenced above.
- Documented interference with activities of daily living: the patient cannot climb stairs without assistance and wakes 3-4 times nightly due to knee pain.
- Nine months of progressive, unrelieved knee pain despite rest.

The guideline further requires "At least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record," listing as examples "Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics," "Intra-articular corticosteroid injections," "Flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises," "Rest or activity modification/limitations," "Supervised physical therapy," and "Assistive device use." The record documents:

- NSAID therapy for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- An intra-articular corticosteroid injection administered 2026-05-19, which provided only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, completed over 8 weeks (2026-05-15 through 2026-07-10, 18 visits), as documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

Taken together, the cumulative course of conservative, non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record spans well beyond 12 weeks (8 months of NSAID therapy alone), and includes multiple modalities specifically listed in the guideline.

I also note that the guideline states: "Prior authorization (PA) is not required for total hip/knee requests treated in an outpatient setting," while "Inpatient TKA and THA requests will require prior authorization." If this request was submitted or reviewed as an outpatient procedure, I ask CountyCare to confirm whether prior authorization — and the associated inpatient-setting documentation requirements — even applied to this request, and if not, to reprocess the request accordingly.

Additional relevant information: there is no active infection, no untreated substance use, the patient's BMI is 29 (not in an obese range), and the patient is a non-smoker.

Deadline note: The notice states that this appeal may be submitted within 180 days of the notice date (by 2027-02-05). I am aware that CountyCare's published Member Rights and Appeals materials also describe a standard 60-calendar-day appeal window, with a 10-calendar-day window to request continuation of services during the appeal. To protect my appeal rights under either standard, I am submitting this appeal now, well within both timeframes, and I am requesting continuation of any previously approved services, if applicable, effective as of the date of this letter.

Enclosed with this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-15 to 2026-07-10, 18 visits)
- MRI report dated 2026-05-30
- Clinic/exam notes documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
- Medication and injection records (NSAID therapy; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-19)
- [Surgeon's letter of medical necessity, if available]
- [Any additional supporting records]

I request that CountyCare overturn the denial and approve the requested partial knee replacement (CPT 27446). If any additional documentation is needed, please contact me at [Phone Number] or [Email Address], or my authorized representative, [Representative Name/Contact, if applicable].

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the applicable decision timeframe in writing.

Sincerely,

_______________________________
Riley Grant
Member ID: W485404613

cc: Marchetti, MD, [Practice Name/Address/Fax]
Enclosures as noted above
